design_detail: Laboratory chemical analysis of commercial products, not of people or cells (the schema has no design for a laboratory analysis of products; 'in-vitro' is the nearest). A German federal risk-assessment institute bought 46 tobacco-free pouch products online between January and May 2021 and measured nicotine (gas chromatography, triplicate), the pH of an aqueous extract and the calculated free-base share, and four tobacco-specific nitrosamines (liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry; one pouch per product, a single screening analysis). It also recorded what the packs printed about nicotine content and warnings. No people, no nicotine uptake and no comparison product (snus, nicotine gum, e-cigarette or cigarette) were measured.
can_establish: How much nicotine, which pH and what calculated share of free-base nicotine were in 44 nicotine pouches (and none in 2 nicotine-free pouches) that a German laboratory bought online in January to May 2021; which tobacco-specific nitrosamines were found at trace levels in some of them and the amounts measured; and how the strength printed on the packs (a milligram figure, a score or a word) related to the measured content.
cannot_establish: What people take in when they use pouches (no uptake, blood or urine measurement; the share extracted in use is taken from another study); whether any pouch is harmful, or less harmful than snus, nicotine replacement products or cigarettes (no health outcome and no other product was measured here); what the market as a whole contains (a convenience sample bought online in 2021, not weighted by sales); the exact nitrosamine amounts (one pouch per product, a single analysis, most results at or near the quantification limit); what other substances the pouches hold (metals, aldehydes, flavouring and other constituents were not measured, as the authors say); or whether products sold now match those bought in 2021.

sample.recruitment: Convenience sample of products (not people): bought January to May 2021 from German online shops or online shops in other countries that ship to Germany; 46 different products from 20 producers (Material and methods › Nicotine pouches, chemicals and standard substances, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: No criteria beyond availability are stated. Two products labelled nicotine-free were included as comparison pouches. The number of packs or batches bought per product is not stated.
sample.attrition: None: all 46 products were measured for nicotine and screened for nitrosamines; the two nicotine-free pouches showed none (Table 2 lists only nicotine-containing products).
sample.selection_effects: Convenience sample, not weighted by sales, bought online in 2021. The authors say the higher contents than in earlier studies of large US brands are partly because they also bought from smaller brands in online shops (Discussion, 1st paragraph). Contents of the most widely sold products and of products sold after 2021 may differ; one product was a free sample with no label at all.

exposure.measurement: Total nicotine by liquid-liquid extraction of one complete pouch (adapted from WHO TobLabNet SOP 4) and gas chromatography with flame ionisation, triplicate; pH of a 10 mL aqueous extract with a calibrated meter, duplicate (the water was not degassed, so dissolved carbon dioxide may have lowered pH); free-base share calculated from pH with the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation (pKa 8.01), not measured. NNN, NNK, NAT and NAB by liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry (ISO 21766:2021) with isotope-labelled standards, one pouch per product, a single screening analysis. Validation: precision below 10%; mean recoveries 102.9% to 126.1% for nicotine and 110.2% to 127.2% for the nitrosamines; detection limits 0.12 (NNN), 0.12 (NNK), 0.22 (NAT) and 0.34 (NAB) ng per pouch (Material and methods; Results › Results of method validation).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Measured product content, not a dose: nicotine 1.79 to 47.5 mg per pouch (median 9.48, interquartile range 5.50 to 16.6); wet weight median 0.643 g (interquartile range 0.455 to 0.718); pH of extract median 8.8 (interquartile range 8.2 to 9.8; range 5.5 to 10.5); calculated free-base share median 86% (interquartile range 62% to 98%) (Results › Nicotine contents, pouch weights and pH of extracts, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 3rd paragraph). No use, route or duration was studied; the products are placed between lip and gum.
exposure.polysubstance: Not applicable (products). Only nicotine, pH and four nitrosamines were measured; other constituents were not.

comparison.controls: Two products labelled nicotine-free are the only reference inside the study. No snus, nicotine gum or lozenge, e-cigarette or cigarette was measured. The Discussion's comparisons with them use figures from other studies (its references 25 to 27) obtained on other bases.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to a product analysis; what was not measured: uptake by people, saliva or urine nitrosamines, other constituents, product ageing, and batch-to-batch variation.

outcomes.instruments: Chemical analyses above; visual inspection of packs for printed nicotine content (milligram per pouch or per gram), a strength score or word, hazard pictograms under EU classification and labelling rules, and warnings for minors and for pregnancy.
outcomes.validity_norms: Method validation is summarised in the main text and detailed in a supplement that was not read. Results for nitrosamines are described by the authors as coming from a single measurement with unsteady precision at the instrument's lower limit (Discussion, 4th paragraph).
outcomes.operationalization: No harm outcome. Content is compared with earlier laboratory studies, with EU thresholds for hazard labels (2.5 and 16.7 mg per gram) and with a European Food Safety Authority reference dose for nicotine in food.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not applicable; no second checker of the label coding is described.

analysis.effect_sizes: No effect sizes. Nicotine per pouch: 1.79 to 47.5 mg, median 9.48 (interquartile range 5.50 to 16.6); two pouches above 40 mg (43.4 and 47.5 mg, both printed as 50 mg per pouch); pH median 8.8; free-base share median 86%. Nitrosamines (ng per pouch, Table 2): detected in 26 of 44 nicotine pouches; NNN in 24 (9 below the quantification limit of about 0.4), highest 12.9 (text) or 13 (table); NNK in 3 (0.5, 0.9, 5.4); NAT in 6 (3 below the quantification limit), highest 2.7; NAB in 5 (2 below the quantification limit), highest 5.6. Counted from Table 1 by the AI reader (not stated in the text): 8 of 44 pouches under 5 mg, 19 above 10 mg, 8 above 20 mg; among the 12 products with a milligram figure and its unit printed, measured content was at or below the printed figure in 11 (up to about 40% below) and above it in 1 (7.09 against 6 mg).
analysis.preregistration_detail: No protocol or registration is mentioned (a laboratory screening).
analysis.selective_reporting: All 46 products are listed in Table 1 and every product with a detected nitrosamine in Table 2. The supplement with validation data and the toxicity-category calculation was not read; Figures 2 and 3 (images) were not read.
analysis.power: Not applicable (no tests). The sample is a convenience sample of 46 products.

interpretation_gap.results_show: In a convenience sample of 46 pouches bought online in 2021, nicotine ranged from 1.79 to 47.5 mg per pouch (median 9.48); most extracts were alkaline with a calculated free-base share around 86%; 15 of 44 nicotine-containing products printed a milligram content, 38 used a score or word for strength, 4 gave no indication, and the contents behind the scores were neither explained nor shared between brands (a product scored 1 of 5 held 7.14 mg while products scored 5 of 5 held 5.72 to 6.66 mg, Table 1); traces of tobacco-specific nitrosamines (up to about 13 ng NNN and 5.4 ng NNK per pouch) were found in 26 products, mostly at or near the quantification limit, from one analysis of one pouch each. Nothing was measured in people, and no snus, nicotine replacement product or cigarette was measured in the same study.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Abstract and Conclusion: some pouches' nicotine content 'alarmingly high'; nitrosamines in the pouches 'of serious concern'; strength labels 'misleading'; pouches 'may potentially be a reduced risk alternative' for people who smoke or use some other oral tobacco products. Discussion: the contents are 'expected to induce and maintain addictive behaviour'; nicotine is toxic on ingestion; with an assumed 60% uptake the lowest-content pouch exceeds a food-regulation reference dose 22-fold; the nitrosamine amounts are much lower than in most cigarettes and in snus but 'still problematic'. Gaps: (1) addictiveness, toxicity and uptake were not measured, and the 22-fold figure is an extrapolation from content using an uptake share from another study; (2) 'serious concern' about nitrosamines rests on trace amounts from a single analysis, while the Discussion itself says the amounts are much lower than in cigarettes and snus; (3) 'misleading' rests on missing and non-comparable strength indicators, not on printed milligram figures being wrong (11 of 12 with a unit were at or below the printed figure, counted from Table 1); (4) the comparison with snus, replacement products and cigarettes uses other studies' figures on other bases, such as smoke yield per cigarette under an intense puffing regime. In the authors' favour, they state the single measurement, the unsteady precision at the lower limit and that the effect on public health is unclear.

timeline.event: Earlier laboratory analyses described in this paper's Discussion (not read): a study of pouches from larger US brands found up to 6.73 mg nicotine per pouch with a similar free-base share, and a manufacturer's study found up to 11.9 mg per pouch and no nitrosamines quantified, with a quantification limit the authors call much less sensitive than theirs.

Laboratory comparison of harmful constituents in two variants of one pouch brand with snus, moist snuff and nicotine replacement products, designed and funded by the maker of that brand, whose employees wrote it; no nitrosamines quantified in the pouches at a limit of 0.01 microgram per gram (see its card).
Scoping review of pouch studies reports analyses of pouch contents from the US and Germany and separates findings by industry funding.

replication.where_it_stands: A single laboratory survey of one set of products. Nobody has re-measured these products; other laboratories have measured other products with different ranges, so the contents are best read as a description of what could be bought, not as a fixed property of pouches.

funding.funder: Intramural funding of the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR), SFP grant no. 1322-772, as printed.
funding.declared_conflicts: Competing interests: none declared (as printed). Provenance: not commissioned; externally peer reviewed.
funding.affiliations_note: All six authors are in the BfR Department of Chemical and Product Safety, Berlin. The Introduction says the institute was asked by the German Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture to assess potential risks of new nicotine pouches, and this chemical characterisation was the first step of an intramural project (Introduction, 5th paragraph). No tobacco, vape or pouch industry funding is stated; the paper notes that most earlier pouch studies were done by manufacturers (Introduction, 4th paragraph).

what_would_settle_it: Replicated measurements (several packs and batches per product, blanks and spiked controls, results shown with and without recovery correction) of nicotine, nitrosamines and other constituents in a sales-weighted sample of pouches, measured in the same laboratory beside snus, nicotine replacement products and cigarettes, and repeated over time; plus measurements in people who use pouches (nicotine uptake, blood and urine markers of nicotine and nitrosamines) beside people who smoke, people who use snus and people who use no nicotine.

domains.note: Convenience sample of 46 products bought online in 2021 from 20 producers; not weighted by sales; packs or batches per product not stated. It describes what could be bought then, not what is mostly used.

Adapted WHO method, triplicate means with standard deviations, validation reported; mean recoveries up to 126.1% with no statement in the main text on correction; extract pH measured in water that was not degassed; free-base share calculated, not measured.

One pouch per product, a single screening analysis; NNN below the quantification limit in 9 of 24 positive products; recoveries 110% to 127%; the authors state unsteady precision at the lower limit. The two nicotine-free products showed none, a weak negative control.

Visual inspection with no second checker described; Table 1 omits the unit for three printed values (20, 20 and 25 mg); the comparison of scores and words with measured content is in Figure 3 (an image, not read).
No snus, replacement product or cigarette was measured; the Discussion's comparisons come from other studies on other bases (per pouch against smoke yield per cigarette).
Two counts differ by one from the tables; evaluative words in the abstract go further than what was measured; the main text itself is open about the single nitrosamine measurement.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated risk-of-bias instrument exists for a laboratory analysis of commercial products (METHODS 5.3), so the editors' checklist is used with domains adapted to this design; the overall judgment cannot be less severe than the worst domain. The nicotine, pH and label results are transparent and sound within a non-representative sample, while the nitrosamine amounts and the comparison with other products are weak. Citable for the measured nicotine content and labelling of these 46 products in 2021 and for traces of nitrosamines in some of them; not for contents of the market as a whole, exact nitrosamine amounts, uptake, harm, or a ranking against snus, replacement products or cigarettes.

key_findings.finding: Sample: 46 pouch products from 20 producers bought January to May 2021 from online shops (German or shipping to Germany); 44 contained nicotine and 2 were labelled nicotine-free. Nicotine, pH, weight and four tobacco-specific nitrosamines were measured; label content and warnings were recorded.
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Material and methods › Nicotine pouches, chemicals and standard substances, 1st paragraph; Results › Product labelling, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Nicotine content ranged from 1.79 to 47.5 mg per pouch, median 9.48 mg (interquartile range 5.50 to 16.6); two pouches (numbers 45 and 46) held more than 40 mg; median pouch weight 0.643 g. No nicotine was detected in the two nicotine-free products.
key_findings.locator: Results › Nicotine contents, pouch weights and pH of extracts, 1st paragraph; Table 1
key_findings.note: A convenience sample; the authors say the higher contents than earlier studies of large US brands partly reflect the inclusion of small online brands.

key_findings.finding: All but one extract was alkaline; median pH 8.8 (interquartile range 8.2 to 9.8; range 5.5 to 10.5); calculated free-base share median 86% (interquartile range 62% to 98%).
key_findings.locator: Results › Nicotine contents, pouch weights and pH of extracts, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 3rd paragraph
key_findings.note: The free-base share is calculated from extract pH with a published pKa, not measured, and the water was not degassed.

key_findings.finding: Labelling: of the 44 nicotine-containing products, 15 printed the nicotine content in milligrams per pouch or per gram; 38 used a score or a word for strength (29 scores, 28 words by the text); 4 gave no strength indication; all but 3 carried a warning for people under 18 and 10 a warning against use in pregnancy. The authors say the contents behind the scores are neither explained nor harmonised between brands.
key_findings.locator: Results › Product labelling, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Results › Relationship between labelled and measured nicotine contents, 1st paragraph; Table 1

key_findings.finding: Some products with a measured content above 16.7 mg per gram (the EU threshold for the 'toxic' pictogram) carried neither that pictogram nor the 'harmful' one. Counted from Table 1 by the AI reader: 16 pouches were above 16.7 mg per gram; 7 of the 44 carried the 'toxic' pictogram, 23 the 'harmful' one and 14 neither.

Tobacco-specific nitrosamines were detected in 26 of the 44 nicotine pouches (none in the two nicotine-free ones): NNN in 24 (9 below the quantification limit), NNK in 3, NAT in 6, NAB in 5. Highest per pouch: NNN 12.9 ng, NNK 5.4 ng, NAT 2.7 ng, NAB 5.6 ng. Results were mostly below or close to the quantification limits and come from a single analysis of one pouch per product.
key_findings.locator: Results › TSNAs in nicotine pouches, 1st paragraph; Table 2; Discussion, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: Comparison figures given by the authors but not measured in this study: up to 1190 ng NNN and 120 ng NNK per pouch of spit-free snus; 2 ng NNN per gram of a nicotine gum in a 2005 study and none in a lozenge; 33 to 323 ng NNN and 40 to 246 ng NNK per cigarette in smoke under an intense puffing regime. The authors conclude the pouch amounts are much lower than most cigarettes and snus, but 'still problematic' next to the traces in replacement products.
key_findings.note: Other studies, other measurement bases (content per pouch against smoke yield per cigarette); not a head-to-head result.

key_findings.finding: Authors' reading: the nicotine content of some pouches is 'concerning' and expected to induce and maintain dependence; with an assumed uptake of 60% of the content, a 60 kg person's reference dose for nicotine in food would be exceeded 22-fold by the lowest-content pouch; pouches are 'under discussion' as a risk-reducing alternative to smokeless tobacco or smoking because of lower toxicant levels, but the overall effect on public health is unclear and the appeal to young people unknown. They call for limits on nicotine, labelling in milligrams per pouch, purity and quality control, and research on uptake.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 1st, 5th and 6th paragraphs and the list that follows; Conclusion, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: Interpretation, not measurement: uptake, dependence and toxicity were not studied here.

key_findings.finding: Earlier laboratory studies described by the authors: up to 6.73 mg per pouch in larger US brands, and up to 11.9 mg per pouch in a manufacturer's study, in which no nitrosamines were quantified in the four pouches investigated (a quantification limit of 10 ng per gram, less sensitive than this study's). The authors say most earlier studies were done by manufacturers.
key_findings.locator: Introduction, 4th paragraph; Discussion, 1st and 4th paragraphs; Key messages box

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract calls some nicotine contents 'alarmingly high' and nitrosamines 'of serious concern'. The paper measured contents only: nothing in people, no uptake, no health outcome, no comparison product. Its own Discussion says the nitrosamine amounts, mostly at or near the quantification limit from a single analysis, are much lower than in most cigarettes and snus.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML, Abstract; Discussion, 4th paragraph; Conclusion, 1st paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite for measured content; the evaluative words are the authors' opinion and carry no measured harm.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says labels of nicotine strength 'on most products are misleading'. The results show missing or non-comparable strength indicators; where a milligram figure with a unit was printed, measured content was at or below it for 11 of 12 products (counted from Table 1), with one product 18% above.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML, Abstract; Results › Product labelling; Table 1
reporting_issues.consequence: The finding is that labels are mostly uninformative or not comparable between brands, not that printed milligram figures were wrong.

reporting_issues.issue: Counts in the text differ by one from the tables: descriptors of strength on '28 products' in Results, 27 rows with a word in Table 1; NNN or NNK 'quantifiable' in '17 products' in the Discussion, 18 in Table 2 (15 with a quantified NNN, 3 with a quantified NNK, none in common).
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML, Results › Product labelling, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 4th paragraph; Tables 1 and 2

reporting_issues.issue: Table 1 gives no unit for three printed nicotine values ('20 mg', '20 mg', '25 mg'); the two '20 mg' products measured 5.72 and 6.24 mg per pouch (17.8 and 18.7 mg per gram) and the '25 mg' product 27.9 mg per pouch.
reporting_issues.consequence: The labelled-against-measured comparison cannot be read from the table for these three; a per-gram label would fit the two '20 mg' products.

reporting_issues.issue: The comparison with cigarettes and snus puts content per pouch beside smoke yield per cigarette under an intense puffing regime and a snus analysis from another study; mean recoveries above 100% (to 126.1% for nicotine and 127.2% for the nitrosamines) are reported without a statement in the main text on whether results were corrected.
reporting_issues.page: publisher HTML, Discussion, 4th paragraph; Results › Results of method validation
reporting_issues.consequence: The ranking against cigarettes and snus is indicative only; the validation supplement was not read.

verification.source_read: publisher full text (HTML), Tobacco Control, https://tobaccocontrol.bmj.com/content/33/2/193: abstract, key-messages box, all sections of the main text, Tables 1 and 2 (read as HTML from the table pop-ups), funding, competing-interest and affiliation statements; Figures 1 to 3 (images), the online supplemental PDF (validation, chemicals and toxicity-category calculation) and the reference list beyond the numbering were not read
